bills.title: MORE American Fuel Act of 2026 (Modernizing Outdated Regulations to Expand American Fuel Act)
bills.status: Reported by EPW with substitute 2026-09-16 (18-1); passed Senate by UC with amendment 2026-09-30; held at the desk in House since 2026-10-05. House passed its own version (H.R.9612, American Enrichment Deployment Act, Fry) 394-3 on 2026-11-09, received in Senate 2026-11-10; same enrichment/notification language carried in the BAAJA nuclear title.
bills.why: Lets an enrichment-facility applicant begin construction at its own risk once NRC dockets the application, drops mandatory uncontested hearings, and requires 15-day notice to state/local/Tribal governments, cutting years off the licensing-to-groundbreaking timeline.

bills.title: Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026
bills.status: S.5653 referred to ENR 2026-09-30; text moved as substitute amendment (SA 6883) to House vehicle H.R.2347: cloture on motion to proceed 73-25 (2026-11-09), cloture 65-31 (2026-11-18), passed Senate with amendment 62-33 (Record Vote 270) 2026-11-19; message sent to House 2026-11-24; awaiting House action before 2026-12-17 sine die.
bills.why: Broad NEPA/CWA/ESA permitting overhaul with judicial-review limits (150-day filing window) plus a nuclear-licensing title that allows NRC licensing without a hearing when none is requested and carries the MORE American Fuel Act enrichment pre-construction and notification provisions.

bills.title: Efficient Nuclear Licensing Hearings Act
bills.status: Referred to EPW 2025-05-14; no further action. House companion H.R.5549 approved by Energy and Commerce 2026-09-02; the hearing provision was folded into the BAAJA nuclear title that passed the Senate 2026-11-19.
bills.why: Amends AEA sec. 189 so NRC may issue a construction permit/license after 30-day notice without holding a mandatory uncontested hearing, removing a fixed delay for enrichment and fuel-cycle facility applications.

bills.title: Nuclear Energy Innovation and Deployment Act of 2026
bills.short: Nuclear Energy Innovation and Deployment Act
bills.status: Referred to Energy and Natural Resources 2026-04-14; no further action.
bills.why: Removes NRC licensing authority over DOE-authorized demonstration reactors and nuclear fuel facilities (including fuel-cycle facilities sited on federal/DOE land) and makes surplus plutonium available for advanced-reactor fuel, opening a DOE-authorization pathway for enrichment and fuel-fabrication projects.

bills.title: Strengthening American Nuclear Energy Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Energy and Natural Resources 2026-03-26; no further action.
bills.why: Gives the force of law to the four May 23, 2025 nuclear executive orders, including EO 14300 (NRC reform with fixed licensing deadlines) and EO 14302 (reinvigorating the nuclear industrial base, which directs DOE to expand domestic enrichment and HALEU capacity).

bills.title: Civil Nuclear Export Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs 2026-08-05; no further action.
bills.why: Adds civil nuclear energy to Ex-Im Bank's China and Transformational Exports Program, exempts that financing from the Bank's exposure cap and raises the default-rate cap from 2% to 4%, expanding U.S. export financing for nuclear fuel and fuel-cycle sales abroad.

bills.title: International Nuclear Energy Act of 2025
bills.status: Reported by Foreign Relations and placed on Senate calendar (Calendar No. 98) 2025-06-18; enacted as Sec. 8366 of the FY2026 NDAA (S.1071, P.L. 119-60, signed 2025-12-18).
bills.why: Creates a Nuclear Exports Working Group, a 10-year civil-nuclear trade strategy with export targets covering nuclear fuel, and directs State/Ex-Im support to displace Rosatom in allied markets, creating demand channels for U.S.-origin enriched uranium.

bills.title: ARC Act of 2026 (Accelerating Reliable Capacity Act)
bills.status: Referred to Energy and Natural Resources 2026-02-10; no hearing or markup.
bills.why: Authorizes up to $3.6B in DOE Loan Programs Office cost-overrun sharing for the first advanced-reactor projects, de-risking the HALEU-fueled reactor fleet that is the demand base for a HALEU enrichment business.

bills.title: Nuclear REFUEL Act of 2025
bills.status: Reported by EPW and placed on Senate calendar (Calendar No. 224) 2025-10-29; awaiting floor action. House companion H.R.3978 approved by Energy and Commerce 2026-09-02.
bills.why: Excludes recycling facilities that do not separate pure plutonium from the AEA 'production facility' definition so they are licensed under the lighter Part 70 process used for enrichment and fuel-fabrication plants; a precedent for fuel-cycle licensing streamlining and a potential competing fuel source.

bills.title: ACE Nuclear Energy Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs 2026-03-26; no further action.
bills.why: Excludes civil-nuclear financing from the Ex-Im Bank default-rate calculation and allows market-rate pay for Ex-Im staff, easing export financing for U.S. nuclear fuel and technology sales.

bills.title: Advancing Research in Nuclear Fuel Recycling Act of 2025
bills.short: Advancing Research in Nuclear Fuel Recycling Act
bills.status: Referred to Energy and Natural Resources 2025-10-16; no further action.
bills.why: Directs DOE to study technologies for converting spent fuel into usable fuel, a long-run alternative supply route that could compete with fresh enriched uranium.

bills.title: Build Nuclear with Local Materials Act of 2026
bills.short: Build Nuclear with Local Materials Act
bills.status: EPW Subcommittee on Clean Air, Climate, and Nuclear Innovation and Safety hearing 2026-05-20; no markup.
bills.why: Requires NRC to allow commercial-grade steel and concrete in non-safety-related structures, lowering construction cost for nuclear facilities generally; the same May 20 hearing aired the Enrichment Licensing Modernization Act draft that became S.5249.

bills.title: ADVANCE Act of 2023 (Accelerating Deployment of Versatile, Advanced Nuclear for Clean Energy Act)
bills.status: Reported by EPW (S.Rept. 118-182, 2024-06-17); enacted as Title II of the Fire Grants and Safety Act (S.870), P.L. 118-67, signed 2024-07-09.
bills.why: Directs NRC to cut fees for advanced-reactor and fuel applicants, set licensing timelines, modernize its mission statement and hearing process, and report on fuel-cycle licensing; it is the statutory base for the enrichment-licensing changes now pending in S.5249/BAAJA.

bills.title: Nuclear Fuel Security Act of 2023
bills.status: Reported by ENR and placed on Senate calendar (Calendar No. 124) 2023-07-11; text added to the Senate FY2024 NDAA by amendment (96-3, 2023-07-27) and enacted as Sec. 3131 of P.L. 118-31, signed 2023-12-22.
bills.why: Establishes the DOE Nuclear Fuel Security Program and HALEU Availability Program and expands the American Assured Fuel Supply, authorizing the federal LEU/HALEU procurement that funded the January 2026 ~$2.7B enrichment awards.

bills.title: Reduce Russian Uranium Imports Act
bills.short: Senate companion to Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act
bills.status: Referred to ENR 2023-03-09; superseded by House companion H.R.1042 (Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act), which passed the Senate by UC 2024-04-30 and became P.L. 118-62 on 2024-05-13.
bills.why: Bans imports of Russian-origin LEU from 2024-08-11, with DOE waivers allowed only through 2027, removing roughly 20% of U.S. enriched-uranium supply and creating the market opening for domestic enrichment capacity.
